links.outcome: Whether large-scale testing reveals failures hidden by small-scale testing
links.effect: Expanding from 1,000 to 10,000 cases characterised rare thrombolysis recommendation errors, including 2.9% persistence when symptoms were documented as >14 days old.
links.quote: Automated expert-level evaluation across 10,000 cases characterised artificial intelligence clinical blind spots hitherto invisible to small-scale testing.

links.outcome: LLM treatment recommendation errors under missing or varied input information
links.effect: Thrombolysis was recommended in 10.1% of cases lacking symptom timing information and persisted (2.9%) even when symptoms were documented as >14 days old.
links.quote: Thrombolysis was recommended in 10.1% of cases lacking symptom timing information and paradoxically persisted (2.9%) even when symptoms were explicitly documented as >14 days old.

links.outcome: Clinically appropriate steroid and thrombolysis recommendations by LLMs for MS cases
links.effect: Appropriate steroid recommendations: Gemini Flash 7.2%, Pro 15.8%, GPT-5-mini 23.5%. Inappropriate thrombolysis: GPT-5.2 9.6%, GPT-5-mini 6.4%, Gemini models <1%.
links.quote: Gemini 3 models had low rates of clinically appropriate steroid recommendations (Flash: 7.2% [95% CI 5.6–8.8]; Pro: 15.8% [13.6–18.1]) compared to GPT-5-mini (23.5% [20.8–26.1]), frequently overlooking contraindications like active infection.

links.outcome: Whether diagnostic competence reflects treatment safety in deployed LLM clinical reasoning
links.effect: All LLMs included MS in the differential in >91% of cases, but treatment safety errors were frequent, so diagnostic accuracy did not associate with treatment safety.
links.quote: However, diagnostic competence did not associate with treatment safety.

unlisted_practices: Automated LLM evaluator validated by blinded subspecialty experts for large-scale synthetic case safety testing

screen.reason: The study conducts a large-scale safety and diagnostic evaluation of frontier LLMs on synthetic clinical cases to identify clinical blind spots and failure modes, but it does not test a specific deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
